sections.title: باب 4 — متن (12)

paras.text: 9. Small number of taxpayers
paras.urdu: 9۔ ٹیکس دہندگان کی قلیل تعداد:
paras.pashto: 9. د مالیه ورکوونکو لږ شمېر

paras.text: About 93 per cent of the total income tax amount is taken from such taxpayers whose number is 3.3 per cent of the total taxpayers.
paras.urdu: کل انکم ٹیکس رقم کا تقریباً 93 فیصد ایسے ٹیکس دہندگان سے لیا جاتا ہے جن کی تعداد کل ٹیکس دہندگان کی 3.3 فیصد ہے۔
paras.pashto: د عاید د ټولې مالیې نږدې 93 سلنه له داسې مالیه ورکوونکو اخیستل کېږي چې شمېر یې د ټولو مالیه ورکوونکو 3.3 سلنه دی.

paras.text: 10. Weak foundations (Weak Base)
paras.urdu: 10۔ کمزور بنیادیں: (Weak Base)
paras.pashto: 10. کمزورې بنسټونه (Weak Base)

paras.text: In our country the base of tax is low and weak, because on one side agricultural income is exempted (Exempted) from income tax, although agricultural income is 20% of gross domestic product (G.D.P); on the other side the industrial sector too has been given many rebates (Rebates) of taxes, e.g. tax holidays, increasing depreciation allowances and loans etc. Moreover, about half of imports are exempt from import duty (Import Duty).
paras.urdu: ہمارے ہاں ٹیکس کی بنیاد پست اور کمزور ہے، کیونکہ ایک طرف تو زرعی آمدنی انکم ٹیکس سے مستثنیٰ (Exempted) ہے حالانکہ زرعی آمدنی مجموعی داخلی پیداوار (جی ڈی پی) 20% فیصد ہے۔ دوسری طرف صنعتی شعبے کو بھی ٹیکسوں کی بہت چھوٹیں (Rebates) دی گئی ہیں، مثلاً ٹیکس ہالیڈے، بڑھتے ہوئے فرسودگی الاؤنسز اور قرضہ جات وغیرہ۔ مزید برآں تقریباً نصف درآمدات امپورٹ ڈیوٹی (Import Duty) سے مستثنیٰ ہیں۔
paras.pashto: زموږ په هېواد کې د مالیې بنسټ ټیټ او کمزوری دی، ځکه له یوې خوا کرنیز عاید له عاید مالیې معاف (Exempted) دی، حال دا چې کرنیز عاید د ناخالص کورني تولید (جي ډي پي) 20% دی؛ له بلې خوا صنعتي برخې ته هم د مالیو ډېرې معافیتونه (Rebates) ورکړل شوي، لکه د مالیې رخصتي، زیاتېدونکي د استهلاک الاونسونه او پورونه او نور. سربېره پر دې نږدې نیمایي واردات له وارداتي محصول (Import Duty) معاف دي.

paras.text: 11. Self-assessment (Self-Assessment) system
paras.urdu: 11۔ خود تشخیصی (Self-Assessment) نظام:
paras.pashto: 11. د ځان ارزونې (Self-Assessment) نظام

paras.text: In Pakistan the self-assessment system of taxes is in force, i.e. the taxpayer himself assesses the tax on his income and pays it to the government. Encouraging results of this system have emerged; e.g. in 1982-83 the number of income-tax payers was 9,77,020, which, increasing, became more than twelve lakh in 2010-11.
paras.urdu: پاکستان میں ٹیکسوں کا خود تشخیصی نظام رائج ہے۔ یعنی ٹیکس دہندہ اپنی آمدنی پر خود ٹیکس تشخیص کر کے حکومت کو ادا کرتا ہے۔ اس نظام کے حوصلہ افزاء نتائج برآمد ہوئے ہیں۔ مثلاً 1982-83ء میں انکم ٹیکس دینے والوں کی تعداد 9,77,020 تھی جو بڑھ کر 2010-11ء میں بارہ لاکھ سے زائد ہو گئی۔
paras.pashto: په پاکستان کې د مالیو د ځان ارزونې نظام رواج دی، یعنې مالیه ورکوونکی پخپله پر خپل عاید مالیه ارزوي او حکومت ته یې ورکوي. د دې نظام هڅوونکې پایلې ترلاسه شوې؛ لکه په ۱۹۸۲-۸۳ کې د عاید مالیه ورکوونکو شمېر 9,77,020 و چې زیات شو او په ۲۰۱۰-۱۱ کې له دولس لکو واوښت.

paras.text: 12. Measures to increase revenue (Revenue)
paras.urdu: 12۔ محاصل (Revenue) میں اضافہ کی تدابیر:
paras.pashto: 12. په عاید (Revenue) کې د زیاتوالي تدابیر

paras.text: The government continuously keeps trying that its revenues should increase, as a result of which these have been increasing at the rate of 19.4 per cent annually. As far as the non-tax receipts (Non-Tax Revenue) of the Government of Pakistan are concerned, continuous increase has been coming in them, but the speed of increase of tax receipts is decreasing.
paras.urdu: حکومت مسلسل یہ کوشش کرتی رہی ہے کہ اس کے محاصل بڑھ جائیں، جس کے نتیجہ میں یہ اوسالانہ 19.4 فیصد کے حساب سے بڑھے ہیں جہاں تک حکومت پاکستان کی غیر محصولاتی وصولیوں (Non-Tax Revenue) کا تعلق ہے۔ ان میں مسلسل اضافہ ہوتا آیا ہے لیکن محصولاتی وصولیوں کے بڑھنے کی رفتار کم رہی ہے۔
paras.pashto: حکومت پرله‌پسې هڅه کړې چې عایدات یې زیات شي، چې په پایله کې یې دا په کلني اوسط د 19.4 سلنې په حساب زیات شوي. تر کومه چې د پاکستان د حکومت غیر مالیاتي وصولۍ (Non-Tax Revenue) پورې اړه لري، په هغو کې پرله‌پسې زیاتوالی راغلی، خو د مالیاتي وصولیو د زیاتېدو سرعت کم پاتې شوی.

paras.text: Proposals for improving the tax system
paras.urdu: نظامِ محصولات بہتر بنانے کے لیے تجاویز
paras.pashto: د مالیاتي نظام د ښه کولو وړاندیزونه

paras.text: We have stated before that the tax system of Pakistan is not satisfactory; therefore, to improve the tax system it is necessary that all those merits be created in it which are in a good tax system and which have been mentioned in the previous chapter. Besides these, for increasing government income the following steps should be taken:
paras.urdu: پیچھے ہم نے بیان کیا ہے کہ پاکستان کا نظامِ محصولات اطمینان بخش نہیں ہے، چنانچہ نظامِ ٹیکس بہتر بنانے کے لیے ضروری ہے کہ اس میں وہ تمام خوبیاں پیدا کی جائیں جو ایک اچھے نظامِ محصولات میں ہوتی ہیں، اور جن کا ذکر پچھلے باب میں ہو چکا ہے۔ ان کے علاوہ سرکاری آمدنی بڑھانے کے لیے مندرجہ ذیل اقدامات کرنے چاہئیں:
paras.pashto: مخکې مو بیان کړل چې د پاکستان مالیاتي نظام ډاډمن نه دی؛ نو د مالیاتي نظام د ښه کولو لپاره اړینه ده چې هغه ټولې ښېګڼې پکې پیدا شي چې په یوه ښه مالیاتي نظام کې وي او په تېر څپرکي کې یې یادونه شوې. سربېره پر دې د دولتي عاید د زیاتولو لپاره باید لاندې ګامونه پورته شي:

paras.text: 1. Increase in direct taxes
paras.urdu: 1۔ براہِ راست ٹیکسوں میں اضافہ:
paras.pashto: 1. په مستقیمو مالیو کې زیاتوالی

paras.text: The share of direct taxes should be increased, so that their burden falls on those people who have the capacity to give.
paras.urdu: براہِ راست ٹیکسوں کا حصہ بڑھانا چاہیے۔ تاکہ ان کا بوجھ ان لوگوں پر پڑے جو دینے کی استطاعت رکھتے ہیں۔
paras.pashto: د مستقیمو مالیو برخه باید زیاته شي، تر څو بار یې پر هغو خلکو ولوېږي چې د ورکولو وړتیا لري.

paras.text: 2. Reduction in the burden of indirect taxes
paras.urdu: 2۔ بالواسطہ ٹیکسوں کے بوجھ میں کمی:
paras.pashto: 2. د غیر مستقیمو مالیو په بار کې کمښت

paras.text: The burden of indirect taxes should be reduced, so that the burden on the poor and middle class becomes less.
paras.urdu: بالواسطہ ٹیکسوں کا بوجھ کم کرنا چاہیے۔ تاکہ غریب اور متوسط طبقہ پر بوجھ کم ہو جائے۔
paras.pashto: د غیر مستقیمو مالیو بار باید کم شي، تر څو پر غریبې او منځنۍ طبقې بار لږ شي.

paras.text: 3. Prevention of tax evasion (Tax Evasion)
paras.urdu: 3۔ ٹیکس چوری (Tax Evasion) کا انسداد:
paras.pashto: 3. د مالیې د غلا (Tax Evasion) مخنیوی

paras.text: The system of enforcing and collecting tax should be better, so that this theft does not happen.
paras.urdu: ٹیکس نافذ کرنے اور اکٹھے کرنے کا نظام بہتر ہونا چاہیے تاکہ یہ چوری نہ ہوں۔
paras.pashto: د مالیې د پلي کولو او راټولولو نظام باید ښه وي، تر څو دا غلا ونه شي.

paras.text: 4. Prevention of concentration of wealth
paras.urdu: 4۔ ارتکازِ دولت کا انسداد:
paras.pashto: 4. د شتمنۍ د تمرکز مخنیوی

paras.text: The different rates of direct taxes should be such that by them the tendency of wealth to become concentrated (Concentration) in a few hands can be stopped.
paras.urdu: براہِ راست ٹیکسوں کی مختلف شرحیں ایسی ہونی چاہئیں، جن سے دولت کے چند ہاتھوں میں مرتکز (Concentration) ہونے کا رجحان رک سکے۔
paras.pashto: د مستقیمو مالیو بېلابېل نرخونه باید داسې وي چې د څو لاسونو کې د شتمنۍ د متمرکز (Concentration) کېدو تمایل ودرول شي.

9. Small number of taxpayers

About 93 per cent of the total income tax amount is taken from such taxpayers whose number is 3.3 per cent of the total taxpayers.

10. Weak foundations (Weak Base)

In our country the base of tax is low and weak, because on one side agricultural income is exempted (Exempted) from income tax, although agricultural income is 20% of gross domestic product (G.D.P); on the other side the industrial sector too has been given many rebates (Rebates) of taxes, e.g. tax holidays, increasing depreciation allowances and loans etc. Moreover, about half of imports are exempt from import duty (Import Duty).

11. Self-assessment (Self-Assessment) system

In Pakistan the self-assessment system of taxes is in force, i.e. the taxpayer himself assesses the tax on his income and pays it to the government. Encouraging results of this system have emerged; e.g. in 1982-83 the number of income-tax payers was 9,77,020, which, increasing, became more than twelve lakh in 2010-11.

12. Measures to increase revenue (Revenue)

The government continuously keeps trying that its revenues should increase, as a result of which these have been increasing at the rate of 19.4 per cent annually. As far as the non-tax receipts (Non-Tax Revenue) of the Government of Pakistan are concerned, continuous increase has been coming in them, but the speed of increase of tax receipts is decreasing.

Proposals for improving the tax system

We have stated before that the tax system of Pakistan is not satisfactory; therefore, to improve the tax system it is necessary that all those merits be created in it which are in a good tax system and which have been mentioned in the previous chapter. Besides these, for increasing government income the following steps should be taken:

1. Increase in direct taxes

The share of direct taxes should be increased, so that their burden falls on those people who have the capacity to give.

2. Reduction in the burden of indirect taxes

The burden of indirect taxes should be reduced, so that the burden on the poor and middle class becomes less.

3. Prevention of tax evasion (Tax Evasion)

The system of enforcing and collecting tax should be better, so that this theft does not happen.

4. Prevention of concentration of wealth

The different rates of direct taxes should be such that by them the tendency of wealth to become concentrated (Concentration) in a few hands can be stopped.

9. Small number of taxpayers

About 93 per cent of the total income tax amount is taken from such taxpayers whose number is 3.3 per cent of the total taxpayers.

10. Weak foundations (Weak Base)

In our country the base of tax is low and weak, because on one side agricultural income is exempted (Exempted) from income tax, although agricultural income is 20% of gross domestic product (G.D.P); on the other side the industrial sector too has been given many rebates (Rebates) of taxes, e.g. tax holidays, increasing depreciation allowances and loans etc. Moreover, about half of imports are exempt from import duty (Import Duty).

11. Self-assessment (Self-Assessment) system

In Pakistan the self-assessment system of taxes is in force, i.e. the taxpayer himself assesses the tax on his income and pays it to the government. Encouraging results of this system have emerged; e.g. in 1982-83 the number of income-tax payers was 9,77,020, which, increasing, became more than twelve lakh in 2010-11.

12. Measures to increase revenue (Revenue)

The government continuously keeps trying that its revenues should increase, as a result of which these have been increasing at the rate of 19.4 per cent annually. As far as the non-tax receipts (Non-Tax Revenue) of the Government of Pakistan are concerned, continuous increase has been coming in them, but the speed of increase of tax receipts is decreasing.

Proposals for improving the tax system

We have stated before that the tax system of Pakistan is not satisfactory; therefore, to improve the tax system it is necessary that all those merits be created in it which are in a good tax system and which have been mentioned in the previous chapter. Besides these, for increasing government income the following steps should be taken:

1. Increase in direct taxes

The share of direct taxes should be increased, so that their burden falls on those people who have the capacity to give.

2. Reduction in the burden of indirect taxes

The burden of indirect taxes should be reduced, so that the burden on the poor and middle class becomes less.

3. Prevention of tax evasion (Tax Evasion)

The system of enforcing and collecting tax should be better, so that this theft does not happen.

4. Prevention of concentration of wealth

The different rates of direct taxes should be such that by them the tendency of wealth to become concentrated (Concentration) in a few hands can be stopped.

paras.text: 5. Income tax on the agricultural class
paras.urdu: 5۔ زرعی طبقہ پر انکم ٹیکس:
paras.pashto: 5. پر کرنیزې طبقې د عاید مالیه

paras.text: Tax should be imposed on agricultural income, because the requirement of justice is that a class with equal income should pay equal tax, whether its income relates to any sector. Thus income tax is closer to justice and equity and becomes the cause of better distribution of income; therefore income tax must be enforced on the agricultural class. Although on the produce of land ushr is collected, this is a kind of zakat which is obligatory on all Muslims of the country having nisab, and income tax is imposed in spite of it; therefore agricultural income cannot be declared exempt from income tax. 5. Income tax on the agricultural class

Tax should be imposed on agricultural income, because the requirement of justice is that a class with equal income should pay equal tax, whether its income relates to any sector. Thus income tax is closer to justice and equity and becomes the cause of better distribution of income; therefore income tax must be enforced on the agricultural class. Although on the produce of land ushr is collected, this is a kind of zakat which is obligatory on all Muslims of the country having nisab, and income tax is imposed in spite of it; therefore agricultural income cannot be declared exempt from income tax. 5. Income tax on the agricultural class

Tax should be imposed on agricultural income, because the requirement of justice is that a class with equal income should pay equal tax, whether its income relates to any sector. Thus income tax is closer to justice and equity and becomes the cause of better distribution of income; therefore income tax must be enforced on the agricultural class. Although on the produce of land ushr is collected, this is a kind of zakat which is obligatory on all Muslims of the country having nisab, and income tax is imposed in spite of it; therefore agricultural income cannot be declared exempt from income tax. Further, since fifty per cent of the land is with big landlords (Big Landlords), therefore, according to the present tax system, by imposing a levy (Tax) on agricultural income a great increase can occur in the income from direct taxes.

6. Wide base of excise tax

Excise tax is imposed on goods made within the country, but eighty-five per cent of the revenues obtained from this head are obtained from only six goods; therefore it is necessary that the scope of excise tax be widened.

By fiscal policy (Fiscal Policy) is meant the strategy adopted by the government in connection with the management of its income and expenditure and their increase and decrease.

Definition of Fiscal Policy

Fiscal policy is defined thus:

“Fiscal policy means such a process and method by which government taxation (Taxation) and government expenditure are used for these purposes: (i) to make the severe ups and downs in trade activities moderate, and (ii) to establish and restore such an economy which is moving towards progress, in which full employment exists, and in which, because of excess demand, there is neither inflation nor deflation.”

(Economic and social) objectives of fiscal policy (Objectives of Fiscal Policy)

The big objectives of the policy of government income and expenditure are as follows:

1. Prevention of business fluctuation (Fluctuation)

Because of different reasons the business trend is sometimes towards “boom” (Boom) and sometimes towards “slump” (Slump), because of which trade conditions become greatly uncertain (Uncertain): obstructions fall in economic development, idleness and unemployment spread. Therefore, for making the economy stable, it is necessary that fluctuations of this kind be prevented. If private expenditure and investment fall, and because of “deflation” (Deflation), i.e. prices becoming less, total expenditure decreases, then the government should make suitable changes in its policy and help in making up this deficiency. And if, because of excessive “optimism” (Optimism) (i.e. keeping hope of good conditions), unrestrained increase keeps occurring in private investment, then to stop it the government should impose tax etc.

مختلف وجوہات کی بناء پر کاروبار کا رجحان کبھی ”تیزی“ (Boom) کی طرف ہوتا ہے اور کبھی ”مندے“ (Slump) کی طرف۔ اس کے باعث تجارتی حالات بڑے غیر یقینی (Uncertain) ہو جاتے ہیں: معاشی ترقی میں رکاوٹیں پڑتی ہیں، بیکاری و بے روزگاری پھیلتی ہے۔ چنانچہ معیشت کو مستحکم کرنے کے لیے ضروری ہے کہ اس قسم کے اتار چڑھاؤ کا سدِ باب کیا جائے۔ اگر نجی خرچ و سرمایہ کاری میں کمی آ جانے سے ”تفریطِ زر“ (Deflation) یعنی قیمتیں کم ہو جائیں اور مجموعی خرچ گھٹ جائے تو حکومت کو چاہیے کہ اپنی پالیسی میں مناسب رد و بدل کر کے، اس کمی کو پورا کرنے میں مدد دے۔ اور اگر زائد از ضرورت ”رجائیت پسندی“ (Optimism) (یعنی اچھے حالات کی امید رکھنا) کے باعث نجی سرمایہ کاری میں بے تحاشا اضافہ ہوتا جائے تو اسے روکنے کے لیے حکومت ٹیکس وغیرہ عائد کرے۔
